session.name: The Leader’s Role in Orchestrating AI-Native platform
session.details: The shift from adding "AI features" to building true, AI-native platforms is the defining operational challenge of the modern enterprise. However, traditional linear models are completely unequipped for this transition.When probabilistic models and autonomous multi-agent systems are forced into legacy, siloed structures, organizations do not get innovation, they get exponential cognitive load, untraceable data lineage, and severe system overload. AI-native platforms are complex adaptive systems that operate on probabilistic outcomes, demanding a leadership shift toward optimizing system health, balancing cognitive load, and managing systemic friction.Key Takeaways - Leaders takeaway learning to protect their AI-native investments ensuring their enterprise platform delivers predictable, compounding net value and achieves steady-state operational equilibrium, rather than collapsing under the weight of its own unmanaged, chaotic complexity. The talk will be centred around the three core pillars - How to connect Systems Thinking, Operations, and Governance with AI-native platforms for best ROI.

AI-Powered Service Operations: Intuit's Incident Management Story
session.details: Managing incidents across thousands of services demands more than traditional playbooks — it requires intelligence, speed, and automation at scale. In this session, we explore how Intuit has transformed its incident management practice by embracing AI-driven solutions built for resilience and continuous improvement.The session covers how Intuit scaled incident management across its entire service ecosystem, and how the team leveraged real-time insights and advanced automation to dramatically improve AWS-related incident detection and resolution. You'll see how simplified detection pipelines drove time-to-detect (TTD) to under 7 minutes — and how an end-to-end automation framework for failover triggering, runbook execution, and recovery orchestration is targeting a nearly 50% reduction in time-to-resolve (TTR) across Intuit's distributed, cloud-native infrastructure.The session will also cover how Agentic AI is reshaping Intuit's root cause analysis process — enabling autonomous, multi-step reasoning that makes post-incident reviews faster, more accurate, and genuinely actionable. Attendees will leave with concrete examples of how AI agents and machine learning can turn complex incident workflows into efficient, resilient operations that keep services available and teams focused on what matters.

session.name: Beyond the Hype: How to Lead, Govern, and Scale AI Responsibly
session.details: AI is no longer an emerging technology—it is a foundational capability reshaping every industry. Yet as organisations race to adopt powerful models and automation, they face a growing challenge: trust. Without strong AI governance, even the most impressive systems can become risky, opaque, biased, or misaligned with organisational values. In this keynote, we'll explore why AI Governance is becoming as essential as cybersecurity and how leaders can build trustworthy, responsible, and resilient AI ecosystems that unlock innovation rather than constrain it. We’ll examine the forces driving the governance imperative—from regulatory shifts and ethical expectations to supply chain risks and the growing dependence on foundation models. Attendees will gain a clear, practical understanding of what “trustworthy AI” really means, the organisational capabilities required to achieve it, and how to navigate a landscape where speed and responsibility must coexist. We’ll look at emerging best practices, real-world pitfalls, and leadership strategies that balance opportunity with oversight. AI success will belong to organisations that embed trust by design, build governance as a core competency, and treat responsible AI not as compliance—but as a catalyst for innovation.

session.name: From blind spots to baselines: building observable, self-healing API ecosystems
session.details: Most enterprise API failures are not sudden — they are slow, invisible, and well-documented in telemetry that nobody is reading. In this session, we explore how organisations can shift from reactive firefighting to proactive performance engineering by building a genuine observability culture around their API platforms. Drawing on real-world experience with large-scale integrations on MuleSoft and Apigee, we will walk through a concrete case study: a production ride-share fare API where p99 latency silently climbed to 340 ms — well above its 100 ms SLA — before distributed tracing pinpointed a single database join in a downstream geocoding service as the root cause. We will show exactly how OpenTelemetry instrumentation was wired across service boundaries, how a Grafana alert fired within seconds of the threshold breach, and how a Redis caching layer was validated live through a canary release — dropping p99 from 340 ms to 18 ms with zero downtime and zero rollback. Attendees will leave with a repeatable framework: what to instrument, what to alert on, and how to use traffic-splitting to validate fixes safely in production — because in high-volume API environments, "test in staging" is not enough.

It explains why separating planning, execution, authorization, and recovery is essential for compliance and resilience, and how non-linear cost behavior in agentic systems requires budget guardrails and outcome-based evaluation to deliver predictable ROI in production.

Infrastructure as Documentation: Designing IaC That Explains Itself
session.details:
Infrastructure as Documentation reframes IaC from “infrastructure scripts” into executable contracts that make intent, boundaries, and assumptions unmistakably clear. Most IaC rots because the why behind the code is invisible; teams inherit modules they don’t understand, reviews become superficial, and governance drifts into side documents no one maintains. This session shows how to design Terraform so that the code is self-documenting, reviewable, and resilient to turnover.
Attendees learn a contract‑first approach that surfaces intent directly through module structure, naming, variables, and outputs. They get a portable pattern library that applies across IaC tools: Terraform is the teaching medium, but the principles translate cleanly to ARM/Bicept, CloudFormation, Pulumi, CDK, and others. A live teardown of a messy Terraform module demonstrates how to uncover hidden intent, refactor for clarity, and align infrastructure with governance without adding bureaucracy.
By the end, participants can design IaC that scales, withstands team changes, improves auditability, and reduces cognitive load for every engineer who touches it.

session.name: Agents and MCP Servers: Are the Electric Sheep Safe?
session.details: We have a new AI attack service. MCP servers are everywhere, and they are the new attack surface. Can the MCP server help protect the electric sheep from rogue agents and bad actors, or are they just another way to attack them? Agents are already being used to automate the software development lifecycle (SDLC), but they also introduce new risks. This talk explores the new attack surface created by MCP servers and agentic AI, focusing on potential vulnerabilities and mitigation strategies. We will discuss how agentic AI can enhance the SDLC while also addressing the security risks it introduces. The talk will cover the role of MCP servers in managing these risks and provide strategies for securing them against potential attacks.Attendee TakeawaysAnswers for the following questions:What does Agentic AI in the SDLC look like?What Security risk do Agentic AI bring to the SDLC?How can MCP servers help with Supply Chain Security?What are the risks of using MCP servers?What are strategies to mitigate attacks on MCP servers?

Every Eng a CTO: Technical Leverage in the Agentic Organization
session.details: A CTO's job is to make difficult technical and organizational decisions, building and tuning up an engine that in turn creates code, infrastructure, and other valuable technical outputs. A good CTO optimizes processes, makes hard calls, and occasionally jumps down to ground level to put out a fire.More and more, the work of ground-level engineers is growing to resemble the description above. A capable engineer in 2026 is increasingly managing a reproducible process that creates infrastructure. The AI-assisted engineer orchestrates agents, moves quickly from decision point to decision point, and develops metainfrastructure. (And, yes, whips out the IDE, text editor, or terminal to put out the occasional agent-generated fire.) In short, the modern agent-assisted engineer is looking a lot like ... a CTO.In this low-BS talk, we'll consider the transformations we're seeing at organizations aggressively adopting not just AI-assisted coding, but also infrastructure that incorporates AI. We'll outline three natural stages of agentification (experiment, pipeline, framework) and present a case study from Chainguard's development and adoption of an agentic framework for reducing drift.We'll then think hard about leverage within an organization and how AI changes organization dynamics, such as by moving engineering time from problems to metaproblems. We'll look at a rough typology of AI adoption among engineers and consider that engineers slow to adopt AI might still be a critical asset. We'll also outline both milestones and pitfalls for your own organization's agentic journey. Come for the hot takes about CTOs, engineers, and organizational leverage, stay for the memes.

session.name: Why not just run it ourselves? Self-hosting AI for fun and for profit
session.details: Your AI costs are skyrocketing, the frontier model providers are changing quality out from underneath you, and meanwhile you’re sending your core IP across the open Internet. How did we end up here? Open-weight AI models have closed the quality gap with proprietary ones and are surprisingly easy to run. In this keynote, Linkerd co-creator and Buoyant CEO William Morgan walks you through what it takes to serve modern LLMs on infrastructure that you control, as a first-class part of your platform: with cost, reliability, and performance measured, managed, and controlled. If you can operate a web service, you can add local inference to your platform. You'll leave this session with the ability to judge whether self-hosting makes sense for your organization, and knowing what to build first if it does.

session.details: APIs often need to deliver images—logos, flags, or product photos. session.name: Break
Hands-On Minimal API: Building Robust Endpoints
session.details: Minimal API is a well-crafted framework, tightly integrated with the ASP.NET Core runtime. Exposing an endpoint can be as simple as a one-liner lambda, but this approach rarely scales beyond small demos or toy projects. A key focus for real-world applications is packaging endpoints into separate classes. While this improves organization, it introduces challenges around dependency injection and model binding. In this session, we’ll cover the technical skills and best practices needed to build realistic, maintainable APIs. You’ll learn how to handle model binding for simple and complex types, leverage dependency injection effectively, manage responses and streaming data, and integrate middleware for cross-cutting concerns. By the end, you’ll know how to scale Minimal API endpoints beyond prototypes into fully structured, high-performing services.

session.name: The End of Documentation: Building an MCP-Based “Living” Platform for Developer Self-Service
session.details:
Many organizations invest heavily in internal documentation and developer portals to help teams provision infrastructure and follow platform standards. However, in practice, developers often struggle to find the right Terraform modules, environment templates, or infrastructure identifiers within internal wikis and documentation systems.
This talk introduces an alternative approach: using Model Context Protocol (MCP) to transform an Internal Developer Platform into a conversational, context-aware interface. Instead of searching through documentation, developers can interact with an AI-powered agent that understands infrastructure context through MCP.
For example, a developer could simply request: “Provision a development environment using the standard PCI-compliant template,” and the agent can interpret the request, retrieve the relevant infrastructure metadata, and guide or automate the provisioning workflow.
The session will briefly explore how MCP can expose infrastructure metadata and platform standards directly to intelligent agents, effectively creating an “Infrastructure-as-Context” layer. This approach enables faster developer self-service while maintaining governance, security, and platform consistency.
Attendees will gain insight into how conversational interfaces and contextual infrastructure data can reduce operational friction and improve developer productivity without sacrificing control.

session.details: AI agents are becoming first-class API consumers and far less forgiving than humans. Today, contract-first design isn’t just a best practice; it’s the only way to keep your APIs discoverable, predictable, and safe for autonomous orchestration.This session focuses on how OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, and domain‑level contracts support agent‑ready systems by enabling unambiguous interfaces and encoded intents. We will detail how to build governance pipelines for scalable teams and provide a blueprint for making APIs legible to humans and machines.

Which foundation model should I use? How do I run inference on my model? How do I connect my model to agents (safely)?The key to navigating this emerging path is adopting the flexibility, transparency, and collaboration of open source that many of us are familiar with. We'll demo the critical aspects of AI feature implementation, showing inference (ollama/vLLM), sandboxing (OpenShell), observability (OpenTelemetry/MLflow), and more. A strategic evolution is overdue.This session introduces Platform Engineering 2.0: an AI-native, autonomous, and business-aligned framework that expands the platform's reach beyond developersto every persona who touches it. You'll learn how PE 2.0 weaves FinOps, security, and composability directly into the platform — making it adaptive rather than bolted-on — and how AI changes what the platform can do for your organization.You'll leave with actionable recommendations for executives and platform engineers alike — including how to build a PE 2.0 business case that reframes the platform as strategic infrastructure, tied directly to developer velocity, cloud cost reduction, and AI readiness.

Breaking Down an LLM for Its Parts
session.details: AI has been around for many years, we’ve been using text to speech and speech to text for over a decade, Siri, Alexa etc., cameras could follow faces a decade ago. However, the major change was just two years ago when Generative Pre-trained Transformers emerged for public use, yes GPT. These are Large Language Models (LLMs) but just for us geeks, are the open source LLMs like Phi 3.5, Qwen 2.5, Llama 3.2 and Mistral, these are advancing so fast I fear even this abstract will be out of date. ​John will pull these LLMs apart to show the internal workings, demonstrate some cool features and help you better understand how they work, what they’re good at and what they’re not good at and why. From vocabulary, tokenisation and embeddings to attention heads, quantisation and performance. We’ll be running everything locally and will try some German in the LLMs too, simple code yet fascinating results. If you get change to download “ollama” (.com) and one or more of the models mentioned above on your laptop, please bring it along.

session.name: AI Trustworthy by Design: A Practical Path to ISO/IEC 42001 and Other AI Governance Standards
session.details: AI is rapidly transforming products, teams and entire organisations—but without a robust governance framework, innovation can easily outpace responsibility. In this talk, we explore how to turn Responsible AI principles into concrete, operational practices using the new ISO/IEC 42001 standard for AI Management Systems. Attendees will learn how to move beyond policies on paper and build governance that is actionable, measurable and aligned with real-world development workflows. We’ll break down the core components of ISO 42001, including risk controls, accountability structures, documentation requirements, transparency mechanisms, and continuous monitoring. Through practical examples, we’ll show how engineering teams, product owners, legal, and leadership can collaborate to embed Responsible AI across the entire lifecycle—from model selection and data governance to deployment and post-release oversight. Whether you’re an engineer trying to make sense of compliance, a leader defining your AI strategy, or a practitioner looking for a pragmatic blueprint, you’ll leave with a clear understanding of how to implement responsible, scalable and audit-ready AI governance that accelerates—not slows—innovation.

Attendees will learn how MCP standardizes interactions between AI models and external systems, improving grounding, interoperability, and reliability. The talk will also cover practical A2A design patterns where multiple AI agents collaborate, delegate tasks, and share contextual memory to solve complex workflows. Through real-world demonstrations using frameworks such as LangChain and LangGraph, participants will gain hands-on insights into building production-ready multi-agent applications. The session will additionally address enterprise concerns including governance, security, scalability, and operational best practices, particularly within regulated industries such as financial services.

session.name: From Discovery to API with AI

session.name: Break
AI - Is it a threat, tool, or transformation partner?
session.details: Artificial Intelligence (AI) stands at a pivotal point in global technological evolution simultaneously perceived as a threat, a tool, and a transformation partner. As a threat, AI raises legitimate concerns around automation-driven job displacement, ethical risks, bias amplification, and the erosion of human agency in critical decision systems. As a tool, it enables unprecedented operational efficiency, analytical capability, and productivity through data-driven insights and automation of complex cognitive tasks. Most critically, as a transformation partner, AI represents a co-evolutionary force reshaping business models, empowering human creativity, and redefining the nature of work and leadership. This triadic lens underscores the importance of governance, transparency, and strategic collaboration to ensure that AI’s transformative potential aligns with human values and institutional resilience. The future of AI integration will be determined not by the technology alone, but by how thoughtfully societies balance these dimensions in pursuit of trusted, human-centric innovation.

session.longAbstract:
This bootcamp gives you a practical, end-to-end understanding of modern platform engineering and Internal Developer Platforms (IDPs). You will begin by exploring the fundamentals of platform ecosystems—user needs, value streams, feedback loops, and organisational constraints—and then progress to advanced topics such as platform pattern languages, DSRP systems thinking, flow optimisation, and designing safe, incremental change.

Through hands-on mapping sessions, you will build real artefacts such as Wardley Maps, OODA loops, 3-axis value-flow maps, and future-state capability designs. You will gain practical experience analysing your own organisation’s delivery landscape, identifying friction points, and shaping platform improvements that developers will actually adopt.

By the end of the bootcamp, you will have a clear understanding of how to design, evolve, and communicate a platform as a product. You will be able to articulate user needs, reduce cognitive load, shape feedback loops, and create a value-aligned roadmap that balances autonomy, governance, and reliability.

You will be well-prepared to contribute to— or lead—platform engineering initiatives in cloud-based or regulated enterprise environments, and to engage confidently in discussions about platform strategy, developer experience, and internal platform architecture.

Agenda Day 1

1. Understanding Your Platform Ecosystem

  • We begin by establishing a clear picture of your current platform and delivery landscape

  • Each participant will map their own developer users, value chains, capabilities, and dependencies

  • Using tools like User Needs Mapping and Wardley Mapping, you will visualise how your platform fits into your wider organisational system

2. Mapping Flow and Feedback Loops

  • Delivery flow depends on fast, reliable feedback, so you will learn to identify where loops break or slow down

  • You will explore real-world friction points such as bottlenecks, hand-offs, cognitive load, and regulatory constraints

  • We will apply OODA loops to model how your teams observe, orient, decide, and act when delivering software

  • Understanding these loops provides the foundation for diagnosing platform friction and designing improvements

  • You will build your first OODA Loop Canvas for your platform

3. Introducing Platform-as-Product Thinking

  • Platforms succeed when treated as products, not internal tooling, so we introduce the core principles of product thinking for IDPs

  • You will identify your key developer journeys and examine how platform capabilities support or impede them

  • We explore what “developer experience” means in practice and how to measure and improve it

  • This sets the stage for designing capabilities that developers actually want to adopt

4. IDP Pattern Language: Foundations of Good Platform Design

  • You will learn the essential building blocks of Internal Developer Platforms

  • Concepts include Golden Paths, self-service, guardrails, abstraction layers, composability, and observability

  • We discuss why some abstractions empower developers while others restrict them

  • This section provides a shared language for discussing platform design decisions across teams

5. Organisational Forces and Architecture

  • We examine Conway’s Law and how organisational boundaries shape the effectiveness of platform teams

  • You will identify mismatches between team structure, platform design, and expected outcomes

  • We explore common failure modes caused by unclear ownership, overlapping responsibilities, or tool sprawl

  • Understanding these forces is key to aligning architecture, governance, and delivery practices

6. Synthesis Mapping Session

  • You will bring together all the mapping tools introduced during the day

  • Participants create a first-pass User Needs Map, a value-flow heat map, and an initial platform review

  • This process highlights where the platform is working well and where change will have the highest impact

We close Day 1 by identifying a small experiment that each participant could run immediately.

session.name: When AI agents go rogue: DevOps lessons from the rise of polymorphic AI
session.details: As AI agents gain the ability to plan, adapt, and even rewrite themselves, they introduce both new power and new risk to software delivery. This talk looks at real incidents and emerging research to show how polymorphic agents can reconfigure behavior, bypass constraints, and challenge assumptions about “safe” automation. Attendees will learn to recognize red flags and rethink quality in a world where tools don’t just follow instructions - they evolve.

session.name: Every Eng a CTO: Technical Leverage in the Agentic Organization
session.details: A CTO's job is to make difficult technical and organizational decisions, building and tuning up an engine that in turn creates code, infrastructure, and other valuable technical outputs. A good CTO optimizes processes, makes hard calls, and occasionally jumps down to ground level to put out a fire.More and more, the work of ground-level engineers is growing to resemble the description above. A capable engineer in 2026 is increasingly managing a reproducible process that creates infrastructure. The AI-assisted engineer orchestrates agents, moves quickly from decision point to decision point, and develops metainfrastructure. (And, yes, whips out the IDE, text editor, or terminal to put out the occasional agent-generated fire.) In short, the modern agent-assisted engineer is looking a lot like ... a CTO.In this low-BS talk, we'll consider the transformations we're seeing at organizations aggressively adopting not just AI-assisted coding, but also infrastructure that incorporates AI. We'll outline three natural stages of agentification (experiment, pipeline, framework) and present a case study from Chainguard's development and adoption of an agentic framework for reducing drift.We'll then think hard about leverage within an organization and how AI changes organization dynamics, such as by moving engineering time from problems to metaproblems. We'll look at a rough typology of AI adoption among engineers and consider that engineers slow to adopt AI might still be a critical asset. We'll also outline both milestones and pitfalls for your own organization's agentic journey. Come for the hot takes about CTOs, engineers, and organizational leverage, stay for the memes.

session.name: Why not just run it ourselves? Self-hosting AI for fun and for profit
session.details: Your AI costs are skyrocketing, the frontier model providers are changing quality out from underneath you, and meanwhile you’re sending your core IP across the open Internet. How did we end up here? Open-weight AI models have closed the quality gap with proprietary ones and are surprisingly easy to run. In this keynote, Linkerd co-creator and Buoyant CEO William Morgan walks you through what it takes to serve modern LLMs on infrastructure that you control, as a first-class part of your platform: with cost, reliability, and performance measured, managed, and controlled. If you can operate a web service, you can add local inference to your platform. You'll leave this session with the ability to judge whether self-hosting makes sense for your organization, and knowing what to build first if it does.

session.name: Building with Open Source AI: A Crash Course
session.details: Thanks to open source, alternatives exist to hitting proprietary, closed-source model providers APIs. Developers and enterprises are saving costs and prioritizing privacy, as they build, test, and deploy their own open models. However, this journey can feel overwhelming. Which foundation model should I use? How do I run inference on my model? How do I connect my model to agents (safely)?The key to navigating this emerging path is adopting the flexibility, transparency, and collaboration of open source that many of us are familiar with. We'll demo the critical aspects of AI feature implementation, showing inference (ollama/vLLM), sandboxing (OpenShell), observability (OpenTelemetry/MLflow), and more. Join us as we get hands-on with language models and use open technologies to control our own AI journey.

session.details: Managing incidents across thousands of services demands more than traditional playbooks — it requires intelligence, speed, and automation at scale. In this session, we explore how Intuit has transformed its incident management practice by embracing AI-driven solutions built for resilience and continuous improvement.The session covers how Intuit scaled incident management across its entire service ecosystem, and how the team leveraged real-time insights and advanced automation to dramatically improve AWS-related incident detection and resolution. You'll see how simplified detection pipelines drove time-to-detect (TTD) to under 7 minutes — and how an end-to-end automation framework for failover triggering, runbook execution, and recovery orchestration is targeting a nearly 50% reduction in time-to-resolve (TTR) across Intuit's distributed, cloud-native infrastructure.The session will also cover how Agentic AI is reshaping Intuit's root cause analysis process — enabling autonomous, multi-step reasoning that makes post-incident reviews faster, more accurate, and genuinely actionable. Attendees will leave with concrete examples of how AI agents and machine learning can turn complex incident workflows into efficient, resilient operations that keep services available and teams focused on what matters.

session.name: Beyond the Hype: How to Lead, Govern, and Scale AI Responsibly
session.details: AI is no longer an emerging technology—it is a foundational capability reshaping every industry. Yet as organisations race to adopt powerful models and automation, they face a growing challenge: trust. Without strong AI governance, even the most impressive systems can become risky, opaque, biased, or misaligned with organisational values. In this keynote, we'll explore why AI Governance is becoming as essential as cybersecurity and how leaders can build trustworthy, responsible, and resilient AI ecosystems that unlock innovation rather than constrain it. We’ll examine the forces driving the governance imperative—from regulatory shifts and ethical expectations to supply chain risks and the growing dependence on foundation models. Attendees will gain a clear, practical understanding of what “trustworthy AI” really means, the organisational capabilities required to achieve it, and how to navigate a landscape where speed and responsibility must coexist. We’ll look at emerging best practices, real-world pitfalls, and leadership strategies that balance opportunity with oversight. AI success will belong to organisations that embed trust by design, build governance as a core competency, and treat responsible AI not as compliance—but as a catalyst for innovation.

session.name: From blind spots to baselines: building observable, self-healing API ecosystems
session.details: Most enterprise API failures are not sudden — they are slow, invisible, and well-documented in telemetry that nobody is reading. In this session, we explore how organisations can shift from reactive firefighting to proactive performance engineering by building a genuine observability culture around their API platforms. Drawing on real-world experience with large-scale integrations on MuleSoft and Apigee, we will walk through a concrete case study: a production ride-share fare API where p99 latency silently climbed to 340 ms — well above its 100 ms SLA — before distributed tracing pinpointed a single database join in a downstream geocoding service as the root cause. We will show exactly how OpenTelemetry instrumentation was wired across service boundaries, how a Grafana alert fired within seconds of the threshold breach, and how a Redis caching layer was validated live through a canary release — dropping p99 from 340 ms to 18 ms with zero downtime and zero rollback. Attendees will leave with a repeatable framework: what to instrument, what to alert on, and how to use traffic-splitting to validate fixes safely in production — because in high-volume API environments, "test in staging" is not enough.

session.name: From Agents to Systems: Orchestration, Recovery, and Economics
session.details: Agentic AI shows strong promise in BFSI, but production deployments surface challenges that go far beyond model performance. This talk shares real-world lessons from deploying multi-agent systems in regulated environments, focusing on three critical areas: reliable orchestration across legacy systems, recovery through verification and repair agents, and the economics of autonomous execution. It explains why separating planning, execution, authorization, and recovery is essential for compliance and resilience, and how non-linear cost behavior in agentic systems requires budget guardrails and outcome-based evaluation to deliver predictable ROI in production.

session.name: Roundtable Discussion at the AI Platform Engineering Day
session.details: In this panel-style session, you will have the opportunity to discuss some of the day’s most interesting questions with speakers and fellow participants. Guided by Garima Bajpai, the conversation will explore governance, responsible AI scaling, AI frameworks, agents, and other key topics in AI-native Platform Engineering.Join us to learn from the experts, exchange perspectives, and share your own experiences.

session.name: Infrastructure as Documentation: Designing IaC That Explains Itself
session.details:
Infrastructure as Documentation reframes IaC from “infrastructure scripts” into executable contracts that make intent, boundaries, and assumptions unmistakably clear. Most IaC rots because the why behind the code is invisible; teams inherit modules they don’t understand, reviews become superficial, and governance drifts into side documents no one maintains. This session shows how to design Terraform so that the code is self-documenting, reviewable, and resilient to turnover.
Attendees learn a contract‑first approach that surfaces intent directly through module structure, naming, variables, and outputs. They get a portable pattern library that applies across IaC tools: Terraform is the teaching medium, but the principles translate cleanly to ARM/Bicept, CloudFormation, Pulumi, CDK, and others. A live teardown of a messy Terraform module demonstrates how to uncover hidden intent, refactor for clarity, and align infrastructure with governance without adding bureaucracy.
By the end, participants can design IaC that scales, withstands team changes, improves auditability, and reduces cognitive load for every engineer who touches it.

session.name: Engineering Interactive AI with WebMCP and MCP Apps
session.details: The era of "text-in, text-out" AI is ending. As developers, we are no longer satisfied with LLMs that simply talk; we need them to act, render, and integrate seamlessly into our web ecosystems. But how do you bridge the gap between a local AI protocol and a production-grade browser environment? In this session, we’ll dive into the cutting edge of the Model Context Protocol (MCP) to transform static chats into dynamic application hubs. We will explore the WebMCP protocol and unlock the power of MCP Apps protocol. Join me to learn how to stop building "chatbots" and start engineering the next generation of interactive AI platforms.

session.name: The Future of API Documentation: Interactive, Executable, and AI‑Navigable
session.details: API documentation is being reinvented. Static pages are giving way to interactive, executable, AI‑navigable experiences, and teams that don’t adapt will be left behind.This talk focuses on practical strategies for next-generation API documentation, including contract-driven generation, executable examples, semantic search, and AI-assisted navigation. Gain actionable steps to begin building human- and agent-ready API docs for the next five years.

session.name: Agents and MCP Servers: Are the Electric Sheep Safe?
session.details: We have a new AI attack service. MCP servers are everywhere, and they are the new attack surface. Can the MCP server help protect the electric sheep from rogue agents and bad actors, or are they just another way to attack them? Agents are already being used to automate the software development lifecycle (SDLC), but they also introduce new risks. This talk explores the new attack surface created by MCP servers and agentic AI, focusing on potential vulnerabilities and mitigation strategies. We will discuss how agentic AI can enhance the SDLC while also addressing the security risks it introduces. The talk will cover the role of MCP servers in managing these risks and provide strategies for securing them against potential attacks.Attendee TakeawaysAnswers for the following questions:What does Agentic AI in the SDLC look like?What Security risk do Agentic AI bring to the SDLC?How can MCP servers help with Supply Chain Security?What are the risks of using MCP servers?What are strategies to mitigate attacks on MCP servers?

session.name: Images in APIs: Databases, Blobs, and Practices
session.details: APIs often need to deliver images—logos, flags, or product photos. At first glance, storing everything in Azure Blob Storage seems obvious, but there are trade-offs in performance, cost, and maintainability. While cloud storage like Azure Blob Storage seems like the obvious choice, databases—an apparently old-fashioned approach—still offer valid advantages for consistency, transactions, and simplicity. This talk explores when to use databases, file systems, or cloud storage, how to structure endpoints, handle caching, and integrate CDNs. Using practical C# examples, you’ll see how to build APIs that serve images efficiently, reliably, and maintainably.

session.name: Building Trusted AI with API-Driven Enterprise Architectures: From Data Governance to Intelligent Automation
session.details: As organizations rapidly adopt AI and intelligent automation, the quality, consistency, and governance of data have become critical success factors. APIs serve as the backbone connecting enterprise systems, data platforms, and AI services, yet many organizations struggle with fragmented architectures, inconsistent data, and governance challenges that limit AI effectiveness.This session explores how modern API-driven architectures can enable trusted AI at enterprise scale. Drawing from real-world experiences across financial services, healthcare, and large-scale digital transformation initiatives, the presentation will demonstrate how organizations can build resilient API ecosystems, integrate governed master data, and implement event-driven architectures that support AI-powered applications.Attendees will learn practical approaches for combining APIs, streaming platforms, data governance frameworks, and cloud-native services to create scalable and trustworthy AI solutions while ensuring data quality, lineage, security, and compliance across distributed enterprise environments.

session.name: Hands-On Minimal API: Building Robust Endpoints
session.details: Minimal API is a well-crafted framework, tightly integrated with the ASP.NET Core runtime. Exposing an endpoint can be as simple as a one-liner lambda, but this approach rarely scales beyond small demos or toy projects. A key focus for real-world applications is packaging endpoints into separate classes. While this improves organization, it introduces challenges around dependency injection and model binding. In this session, we’ll cover the technical skills and best practices needed to build realistic, maintainable APIs. You’ll learn how to handle model binding for simple and complex types, leverage dependency injection effectively, manage responses and streaming data, and integrate middleware for cross-cutting concerns. By the end, you’ll know how to scale Minimal API endpoints beyond prototypes into fully structured, high-performing services.

session.name: The End of Documentation: Building an MCP-Based “Living” Platform for Developer Self-Service
session.details:
Many organizations invest heavily in internal documentation and developer portals to help teams provision infrastructure and follow platform standards. However, in practice, developers often struggle to find the right Terraform modules, environment templates, or infrastructure identifiers within internal wikis and documentation systems.
This talk introduces an alternative approach: using Model Context Protocol (MCP) to transform an Internal Developer Platform into a conversational, context-aware interface. Instead of searching through documentation, developers can interact with an AI-powered agent that understands infrastructure context through MCP.
For example, a developer could simply request: “Provision a development environment using the standard PCI-compliant template,” and the agent can interpret the request, retrieve the relevant infrastructure metadata, and guide or automate the provisioning workflow.
The session will briefly explore how MCP can expose infrastructure metadata and platform standards directly to intelligent agents, effectively creating an “Infrastructure-as-Context” layer. This approach enables faster developer self-service while maintaining governance, security, and platform consistency.
Attendees will gain insight into how conversational interfaces and contextual infrastructure data can reduce operational friction and improve developer productivity without sacrificing control.

session.name: Contract‑First APIs in the Age of AI Agents
session.details: AI agents are becoming first-class API consumers and far less forgiving than humans. Today, contract-first design isn’t just a best practice; it’s the only way to keep your APIs discoverable, predictable, and safe for autonomous orchestration.This session focuses on how OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, and domain‑level contracts support agent‑ready systems by enabling unambiguous interfaces and encoded intents. We will detail how to build governance pipelines for scalable teams and provide a blueprint for making APIs legible to humans and machines.

session.name: Breaking Down an LLM for Its Parts
session.details: AI has been around for many years, we’ve been using text to speech and speech to text for over a decade, Siri, Alexa etc., cameras could follow faces a decade ago. However, the major change was just two years ago when Generative Pre-trained Transformers emerged for public use, yes GPT. These are Large Language Models (LLMs) but just for us geeks, are the open source LLMs like Phi 3.5, Qwen 2.5, Llama 3.2 and Mistral, these are advancing so fast I fear even this abstract will be out of date. ​John will pull these LLMs apart to show the internal workings, demonstrate some cool features and help you better understand how they work, what they’re good at and what they’re not good at and why. From vocabulary, tokenisation and embeddings to attention heads, quantisation and performance. We’ll be running everything locally and will try some German in the LLMs too, simple code yet fascinating results. If you get change to download “ollama” (.com) and one or more of the models mentioned above on your laptop, please bring it along.

session.name: AI Trustworthy by Design: A Practical Path to ISO/IEC 42001 and Other AI Governance Standards
session.details: AI is rapidly transforming products, teams and entire organisations—but without a robust governance framework, innovation can easily outpace responsibility. In this talk, we explore how to turn Responsible AI principles into concrete, operational practices using the new ISO/IEC 42001 standard for AI Management Systems. Attendees will learn how to move beyond policies on paper and build governance that is actionable, measurable and aligned with real-world development workflows. We’ll break down the core components of ISO 42001, including risk controls, accountability structures, documentation requirements, transparency mechanisms, and continuous monitoring. Through practical examples, we’ll show how engineering teams, product owners, legal, and leadership can collaborate to embed Responsible AI across the entire lifecycle—from model selection and data governance to deployment and post-release oversight. Whether you’re an engineer trying to make sense of compliance, a leader defining your AI strategy, or a practitioner looking for a pragmatic blueprint, you’ll leave with a clear understanding of how to implement responsible, scalable and audit-ready AI governance that accelerates—not slows—innovation.

session.name: When You Don't Need an LLM: Deterministic Intelligence for Real World Apps
session.details: We want our modern apps to feel intelligent, but many teams assume that means adopting large language models. In reality, most real-world problems are better handled using deterministic tools that are fast, predictable, and easy to test. This talk shows how developers can add intelligent behavior to their applications using tools like constraint solving and optimization. We will walk through a real API implementation, show how a deterministic engine produces correct results that an LLM cannot guarantee, and give developers practical intuition for when these tools are the right fit compared to model-driven approaches.

session.name: Building Intelligent Systems with Model Context Protocol (MCP) and Agent-to-Agent (A2A) Applications
session.details: As AI systems become increasingly sophisticated, enabling reliable communication between models, tools, and autonomous agents is becoming essential for enterprise AI adoption. This session explores the Model Context Protocol (MCP) and Agent-to-Agent (A2A) architectures that enable scalable, context-aware AI ecosystems. Attendees will learn how MCP standardizes interactions between AI models and external systems, improving grounding, interoperability, and reliability. The talk will also cover practical A2A design patterns where multiple AI agents collaborate, delegate tasks, and share contextual memory to solve complex workflows. Through real-world demonstrations using frameworks such as LangChain and LangGraph, participants will gain hands-on insights into building production-ready multi-agent applications. The session will additionally address enterprise concerns including governance, security, scalability, and operational best practices, particularly within regulated industries such as financial services.

session.name: From Discovery to API with AI
session.details: AI is making code generation cheap. The constraint in API work isshifting to design; how systems are defined, aligned, and governedover time. This talk outlines a practical approach to using AI as adesign collaborator that augments and amplifies human capabilityrather than replacing it. Starting from domain discovery, you’ll seehow AI extracts a shared vocabulary and carries it through OpenAPIdefinitions, documentation, security profiles, and test scripts allending in a working prototype. Throughout the end-to-end example, thefocus is on traceability: maintaining a clear, reviewable line frombusiness intent to running system while sharpening the skills requiredto design well. For architects and decision-makers, this creates aconsistent, reviewable process with measurable outputs. Fordevelopers, it reduces manual effort while strengthening core designskills. The result is a lightweight workflow that accelerates deliverywhile preserving control and capability.

session.name: Making Your APIs AI-Ready
session.details: This session talk outlines five critical shifts organizations canmake to ensure their API ecosystems are machine-ready: Intentionality,Context, Standardization, Discovery, and Adaptability. Drawinginspiration from pioneers like Donald Norman, Douglas Engelbart, RoyFielding, Ted Nelson and Christopher Alexander, Mike Amundsen offers astrategic and actionable framework to help API teams prepare for theinevitable; machine-driven APIs.

session.name: Designing Governance-Aware AI Frameworks for Compliance in FinTech and Insurance
session.details: As enterprises adopt AI in regulated industries, the challenge is no longer only model performance, but trust, auditability, transparency, and operational control. This session explores how governance-aware AI frameworks can help organizations safely move from experimentation to production. Drawing from real-world enterprise architecture experience, I will discuss how rule-based controls, explainability, validation workflows, and human oversight can be embedded into AI-enabled systems to support responsible AI adoption in financial services and insurance. Attendees will learn practical patterns for reducing compliance risk while enabling automation, efficiency, and scalable AI transformation.

session.name: AI - Is it a threat, tool, or transformation partner?
session.details: Artificial Intelligence (AI) stands at a pivotal point in global technological evolution simultaneously perceived as a threat, a tool, and a transformation partner. As a threat, AI raises legitimate concerns around automation-driven job displacement, ethical risks, bias amplification, and the erosion of human agency in critical decision systems. As a tool, it enables unprecedented operational efficiency, analytical capability, and productivity through data-driven insights and automation of complex cognitive tasks. Most critically, as a transformation partner, AI represents a co-evolutionary force reshaping business models, empowering human creativity, and redefining the nature of work and leadership. This triadic lens underscores the importance of governance, transparency, and strategic collaboration to ensure that AI’s transformative potential aligns with human values and institutional resilience. The future of AI integration will be determined not by the technology alone, but by how thoughtfully societies balance these dimensions in pursuit of trusted, human-centric innovation.

session.longAbstract:
This bootcamp gives you a practical, end-to-end understanding of modern platform engineering and Internal Developer Platforms (IDPs). You will begin by exploring the fundamentals of platform ecosystems—user needs, value streams, feedback loops, and organisational constraints—and then progress to advanced topics such as platform pattern languages, DSRP systems thinking, flow optimisation, and designing safe, incremental change.

Through hands-on mapping sessions, you will build real artefacts such as Wardley Maps, OODA loops, 3-axis value-flow maps, and future-state capability designs. You will gain practical experience analysing your own organisation’s delivery landscape, identifying friction points, and shaping platform improvements that developers will actually adopt.

By the end of the bootcamp, you will have a clear understanding of how to design, evolve, and communicate a platform as a product. You will be able to articulate user needs, reduce cognitive load, shape feedback loops, and create a value-aligned roadmap that balances autonomy, governance, and reliability.

You will be well-prepared to contribute to— or lead—platform engineering initiatives in cloud-based or regulated enterprise environments, and to engage confidently in discussions about platform strategy, developer experience, and internal platform architecture.

Agenda Day 1

1. Understanding Your Platform Ecosystem

  • We begin by establishing a clear picture of your current platform and delivery landscape

  • Each participant will map their own developer users, value chains, capabilities, and dependencies

  • Using tools like User Needs Mapping and Wardley Mapping, you will visualise how your platform fits into your wider organisational system

2. Mapping Flow and Feedback Loops

  • Delivery flow depends on fast, reliable feedback, so you will learn to identify where loops break or slow down

  • You will explore real-world friction points such as bottlenecks, hand-offs, cognitive load, and regulatory constraints

  • We will apply OODA loops to model how your teams observe, orient, decide, and act when delivering software

  • Understanding these loops provides the foundation for diagnosing platform friction and designing improvements

  • You will build your first OODA Loop Canvas for your platform

3. Introducing Platform-as-Product Thinking

  • Platforms succeed when treated as products, not internal tooling, so we introduce the core principles of product thinking for IDPs

  • You will identify your key developer journeys and examine how platform capabilities support or impede them

  • We explore what “developer experience” means in practice and how to measure and improve it

  • This sets the stage for designing capabilities that developers actually want to adopt

4. IDP Pattern Language: Foundations of Good Platform Design

  • You will learn the essential building blocks of Internal Developer Platforms

  • Concepts include Golden Paths, self-service, guardrails, abstraction layers, composability, and observability

  • We discuss why some abstractions empower developers while others restrict them

  • This section provides a shared language for discussing platform design decisions across teams

5. Organisational Forces and Architecture

  • We examine Conway’s Law and how organisational boundaries shape the effectiveness of platform teams

  • You will identify mismatches between team structure, platform design, and expected outcomes

  • We explore common failure modes caused by unclear ownership, overlapping responsibilities, or tool sprawl

  • Understanding these forces is key to aligning architecture, governance, and delivery practices

6. Synthesis Mapping Session

  • You will bring together all the mapping tools introduced during the day

  • Participants create a first-pass User Needs Map, a value-flow heat map, and an initial platform review

  • This process highlights where the platform is working well and where change will have the highest impact

We close Day 1 by identifying a small experiment that each participant could run immediately.

  • We start Day 2 by introducing DSRP: Distinctions, Systems, Relationships, and Perspectives

  • You will revisit yesterday’s maps to uncover blind spots and hidden dependencies

  • This provides a rigorous method for analysing complex socio-technical environments

  • DSRP becomes a lens that enhances all further platform design work

2. Constructing a 3-Axis Flow Map

  • We combine User Needs Mapping, Value Stream Mapping, and DSRP into a unified diagnostic model

  • You will map how user needs unfold over time across teams, capabilities, and tools

  • This highlights delays, waste, rework, context-switching, cognitive load, and risk points

  • The 3-axis map becomes the definitive view of your platform’s current state

3. Designing Your Future Platform State

  • Using your diagnostic maps, we shift from analysis to design

  • You will identify the smallest viable changes that unlock significant flow improvements

  • We explore capability increments, migration paths, and safe-to-fail experiments

  • This creates a realistic, evolvable, and technically grounded future-state platform design

4. Building an Impact Roadmap

  • With the future design defined, participants prioritise improvements based on value, risk, and cost

  • We explore sequencing strategies, dependency management, and incremental rollout

  • You will build a value-aligned roadmap that is suitable for communication with stakeholders or leadership

  • This section ensures your platform evolution is intentional rather than reactive

5. Adoption & Influence Strategies

  • A platform only delivers value when developers actually use it, so we focus on the Elephant & Rider model of behaviour change

  • You will identify the emotional and rational adoption drivers specific to your organisation

  • We discuss messaging, internal marketing, documentation styles, and team engagement patterns
    You will create an adoption and influence plan tailored to your context

6. Platform Futures & Final Synthesis

  • We close by exploring emerging trends: AI agents and augmentation, automation loops, self-healing systems, and resilience patterns

  • Each participant updates their platform review based on everything learned

  • You will leave with a clear set of maps, artefacts, and experiments to continue after the workshop

  • Final Q&A and reflection
